notes:
I found good verse-by-verse material from the older commentaries (Ellicott, Pulpit, Gill, Barnes, Calvin, Wesley, Clarke, Keil & Delitzsch, Jamieson-Fausset-Brown, Matthew Henry), from Enduring Word, and from one Catholic commentary (Haydock). There are gaps, listed at the end.

**The main split:** Most of the disagreement in this chapter is about prophecy and the end times, not about denominations. On one side are futurist, premillennial readers (Guzik at Enduring Word, MacArthur at GTY, Gill). On the other are readers who apply the chapter to the church across history or to AD 70 (Calvin, Wesley, Ligonier's Barry Cooper, the Pulpit Commentary). Many older writers take a middle path. For them, Antiochus Epiphanes (the Greek king who desecrated the Jerusalem temple in the 160s BC) is a near "type," a first fulfilment that foreshadows a later, greater one.

---

**v. 1**
- **Traditional reading:** "At that time" means the period of Daniel 11:45, before the wicked king falls. Michael comes to help God's people. Michael's presence doesn't stop the time of trouble; he helps God's people through it. Ellicott links the trouble to the tribulation of Matthew 24:21–22. — https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/daniel-12.html
- **Futurist (Guzik, Enduring Word):** This is a future Great Tribulation, worse than all earlier persecutions of the Jewish people put together. The promise of rescue covers those written in the book, not every last person of Jewish heritage. — https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-12/
- **Reformed (Calvin):** The angel proclaims God to be in general the guardian of his Church, and the promise is limited to the elect. Calvin says many take Michael to be Christ, but the archangel working under Christ also fits. — https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/cal/daniel-12.html
- **Methodist (Wesley):** Just as the Jews had some relief after Antiochus died, a greater deliverance will come when Michael your prince, the Messiah shall appear. The "time of trouble" is the siege of Jerusalem, and "at that time" probably includes all the time of Christ, from his first, to his last coming. — https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/daniel-12.html
- **Pulpit Commentary:** Reads Jesus' use of the verse as being about AD 70: the Jews perished, the Christians were delivered. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/daniel/12.htm
- **"The book":** Jamieson-Fausset-Brown call it the book of God's secret purpose, a picture taken from a list of citizens (Nehemiah 7:5). They also see a double reference: typically, towards the close of Antiochus' reign; antitypically, the time when Antichrist is to be destroyed. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/daniel/12.htm
- **Catholic (Haydock):** Citing Calmet, applies the verse to the Maccabees: Michael protected the Jews, and a small army under Judas freed the country. Citing Worthington, says Michael will also guard the Church against antichrist. — https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/hcc/daniel-12.html

**v. 2**
- **Traditional reading:** This is a distinct reference to the resurrection of the body. The resurrection is individual, not national, as shown by the contrasted fates. "Many" does not rule out "all"; the point is the great number. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/daniel/12.htm
- **Ellicott:** The verse teaches a general resurrection and a resurrection of the unjust as well as of the just. The word "contempt" appears only here and in Isaiah 66:24. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/daniel/12.htm
- **Barnes:** The word "everlasting" is the same in both halves of the verse, as in Matthew 25:46, and it would denote a strict and proper eternity. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/daniel/12-2.htm
- **Calvin:** The Church will be like a dead body until it shall rise again. He takes "many" as meaning all, and says the prophets give no clearer witness to the final resurrection. — https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/cal/daniel-12.html
- **Guzik, on hell:** He uses the verse against the idea that the lost suffer for a while and are then destroyed: The terror of hell never ends. There is not blissful annihilation after some period of punishment. — https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-12/
- **Bible.org (Utley):** He also reads it as a general resurrection, but he points readers to Edward Fudge's book defending annihilationism (the view that the lost are finally destroyed) alongside Erickson's reply. So he treats the question as open to discussion. — https://bible.org/seriespage/daniel-12
- **Moral or national readings:** Gray's Concise Commentary asks whether this is a physical or a moral resurrection and leans to the moral one, in line with Ezekiel 37. — https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/jgc/daniel-12.html. Matthew Henry says rescue from persecution is "a kind of resurrection," as in Ezekiel 37. — https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Dan/Dan_012.cfm
- **Catholic (Haydock):** All shall rise again. It also gives a figurative sense: the Jews who seemed buried will rise and fight. The text is express for eternal happiness or misery. — https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/hcc/daniel-12.html

**v. 3**
- **Ellicott:** "The wise" are the "people who understand" of 11:33, who set an example by staying faithful to the covenant. Compare Matthew 13:43. — https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/daniel-12.html
- **Calvin:** "Those who lead many to righteousness" are especially teachers, but the phrase includes all godly people. "Endued with understanding" means those who hold to the true knowledge of God. Calvin adds that no one can justify another person. God's own work is credited to his ministers, because their teaching brings faith. — https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/cal/daniel-12.html
- **Guzik:** Turning others to righteousness is an investment that lasts forever, unlike most earthly achievements. — https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-12/
- **Bible.org (Utley):** Jesus quotes this verse in Matthew 13:43. It may point to different degrees of reward. — https://bible.org/seriespage/daniel-12
- **Catholic (Haydock):** Citing Worthington, teachers, martyrs and virgins receive an extra reward (an "aureola") on top of the basic joy of heaven. — https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/hcc/daniel-12.html

**v. 4**
- **Ellicott:** "Sealing" means keeping the book safe for the time when its fulfilment makes it clear. "Run to and fro" means searching, so many will anxiously search in this book for knowledge of the manner of God's dealings with His people. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/daniel/12.htm
- **Futurist (Guzik):** Notes that many take this prediction as being fulfilled in the travel and information explosions of modern times. He suggests the growth of prophecy study over the last 150 years shows we are in the time of the end. — https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-12/
- **Calvin:** Sealing means "treasure it," even if most people despise it. "Many shall run to and fro" promises that God will gather many disciples. — https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/cal/daniel-12.html
- **Wesley:** The book was sealed because its fulfilment was far off. People will diligently search these prophecies, chiefly in the gospel age. — https://www.studylight.org/commentary/daniel/12-4.html
- **Pulpit:** The prophecies were not hidden from being read. They were not understood because they had not yet been interpreted. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/daniel/12.htm

**v. 5**
- **Ellicott:** Two heavenly beings appear. Jerome thought they were the angels of Persia and Greece, but of course it is impossible to identify them. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/daniel/12.htm
- **Wesley:** Two angels waiting on Christ. — https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/daniel-12.html
- **Gill:** Angels serving Christ and ready to carry out his orders. — https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/daniel-12.html

**v. 6**
- **Who is the man in linen?** Wesley says Christ, who seemed to stand in the air above the waters (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/daniel-12.html). Gill also says Christ (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/daniel-12.html). Calvin says it may refer to Christ but will not say so firmly (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/cal/daniel-12.html).
- **Ellicott:** The Hebrew word used here for "river" usually means the Nile. It reassures readers that the God who struck the Nile will hold back hostile powers. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/daniel/12.htm
- **Calvin:** One angel questioning another shows that some of God's works are hidden even from angels. That should make us pay closer attention. — https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/cal/daniel-12.html

**v. 7**
- **The oath:** People normally raised only the right hand to swear. Raising both hands gives the words greater weight. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/daniel/12.htm
- **"Time, times and half a time": the main split.**
  - *Futurist (Guzik):* the angel swears that the trouble lasts exactly three and a half years, matching Revelation. — https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-12/
  - *Methodist (Wesley):* "a year, two years and half a year," the same period Revelation calls 42 months or 1,260 days. — https://www.studylight.org/commentary/daniel/12-7.html
  - *Reformed (Calvin):* not to be understood literally but metaphorically, signifying, as I have already stated, an indefinite period. The verse calls for endurance through a long stretch of time. — https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/cal/daniel-12.html
  - *Ellicott:* the measures of time do not match, so it cannot refer to the persecution under Antiochus. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/daniel/12.htm
- **"Shattering the power of the holy people":** Ellicott says the end won't come until persecution seems to have stamped out all that remains of godliness. — https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/daniel-12.html. Guzik says Israel will look completely crushed, and then the Messiah returns to rescue them. — https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-12/. Gill says it is when antichrist finishes scattering the church and the "slaying of the witnesses" is over. — https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/daniel-12.html
- **Matthew Henry:** Links the three and a half years to the length of Christ's public ministry, ending with "It is finished." — https://www.studylight.org/commentary/daniel/12-9.html
- **Catholic (Haydock):** Three and a half years. According to Worthington, all the Fathers agree that the last persecution shall continue no longer. The commentary attacks Protestants who read the figures as years of the papacy. — https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/hcc/daniel-12.html

**v. 8**
- **Ellicott:** Daniel didn't understand, because the answer given was only "time, times and a half." His follow-up question asks which of the wonders comes last before the end. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/daniel/12.htm
- **Guzik:** Even Daniel didn't understand everything, which is a comfort when we have questions about the future. — https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-12/

**v. 9**
- **Ellicott:** "Go your way" means be at peace. It is a gentle rebuke, like the one in John 21:21–22. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/daniel/12.htm
- **Gill:** time is the best interpreter of prophecy. Wesley agrees: They shall not be clearly understood, 'till the event make them good. — https://www.studylight.org/commentary/daniel/12-9.html and https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/daniel/12.htm

**v. 10**
- **Ellicott:** The righteous will be purified while the wicked fall away. Only the wise grasp what tribulation is for. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/daniel/12.htm
- **Calvin:** The three words show that believers need continual cleansing as long as they are clothed in flesh, like clothes worn every day. — https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/cal/daniel-12.html
- **Methodist:** Wesley says trials prepare the church for the bridegroom, as gold and silver are refined (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/daniel-12.html). Clarke says the purified will be fully saved from their sins (https://www.studylight.org/commentary/daniel/12-10.html).
- **Pulpit:** You need to be pursuing holiness to understand God's ways. Its example is Christians leaving Jerusalem before AD 70. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/daniel/12.htm
- **Catholic (Haydock):** The faithful see suffering as a trial of God's servants and a mark of predestination. — https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/hcc/daniel-12.html

**v. 11**
- **Ellicott:** This verse seems to go back to the nearer future, the same event as 11:31. Neither number fits three and a half years without setting the rules of arithmetic at defiance. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/daniel/12.htm
- **Futurist/Baptist (MacArthur, GTY):** The 1,260 days take us to the end of the Tribulation. Then come thirty more days for the judgment of the nations. Forty-five more days for the establishing of the millennial kingdom. — https://gty.org/library/sermons-library/2369/the-abomination-of-desolation
- **Precept Austin:** Of Daniel's three mentions of the abomination, two (9:27 and 12:11) describe the Antichrist and one (11:31) Antiochus. — https://www.preceptaustin.org/pdf/60072/
- **Reformed (Ligonier, Barry Cooper):** Antiochus was the short-term fulfilment. The longer-term one was the Romans under Titus in AD 70, whose armies brought idolatrous images and destroyed the temple. (He covers all three passages in Daniel together.) — https://learn.ligonier.org/podcasts/simply-put/abomination-of-desolation
- **Bible.org (Utley):** Lists three readings: Antiochus IV, Titus in AD 70, or the end times. He suggests the text may be "multi-fulfillment prophecy." — https://bible.org/seriespage/daniel-12
- **Calvin:** The angel deliberately says days instead of years. Though the time may seem endless, it has to be endured. — https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/cal/daniel-12.html

**v. 12**
- **Calvin:** In numerical calculations I am no conjurer. He warns that over-precise calculation weakens the prophecy. — https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/cal/daniel-12.html
- **Gill:** The extra 45 days or years are when the bowls of wrath are poured out and Christ's enemies are removed. He records that many interpreters date the 45 days from the temple's rededication to Antiochus's death. — https://www.studylight.org/commentary/daniel/12-12.html
- **Futurist (Enduring Word):** Guzik places the judgment of the nations from Matthew 25 within the 45 days. Lance Ralston puts it at day 1,335, the start of the Millennium. — https://enduringword.com/in-daniel-12-what-do-the-numbers-1290-and-1335-mean-are-they-related-to-revelation-12/
- **Pulpit:** All the proposed solutions are unsatisfactory, which prove that no solution is possible. — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/daniel/12.htm
- **Catholic (Haydock):** Gives Calmet's link to Antiochus's death and Menochius's idea of a 45-day window for repentance. It closes with Worthington: we are content to go away with Daniel without searching further. — https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/hcc/daniel-12.html

**v. 13**
- **Ellicott:** Daniel will rest in the grave and rise to his "lot," which recalls Joshua dividing the land by lot. One greater than Joshua will share out the heavenly Canaan. — https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/daniel-12.html
- **Wesley:** Daniel will die in hope and rest until the resurrection of the just. Secure a happy lot at the end, and be content with your present one. — https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/daniel-12.html
- **Guzik:** Each of us has our own calling to finish, so we shouldn't become obsessed with future events. — https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-12/
- **Gill:** Quotes a Jewish paraphrase (Jacchiades): rest in paradise, then rise at the resurrection. — https://www.studylight.org/commentary/daniel/12-13.html

---

**Critical scholarship, as reported by conservative writers:** Keil & Delitzsch reject the view of those who dispute the genuineness of the book. On that view, a "pseudo-Daniel" expected the resurrection right after Antiochus died. — https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/kdo/daniel-12.html. A Bible Hub Q&A replies that the Dead Sea Scrolls show the text came before Antiochus. — https://biblehub.com/q/Daniel_12_11_and_abomination_link.htm. These descriptions come from the view's opponents, not from critical scholars themselves.

**What I couldn't find:**
- Any bibleodyssey.org or netbible.org notes, so mainstream modern scholarship is not represented in its own words.
- Lutheran (lcms.org, 1517.org), Orthodox (oca.org), or newadvent.org/catholic.com pages. The only Catholic source is Haydock.
- Pentecostal sources apart from Enduring Word, the one site I read from that category.
- Anything on prosperity, word of faith or hyper-grace teaching about this chapter.
